title: Conversation-velocity latency snapshots by model & route (streaming vs non-streaming)
creator: Avery Chen
description: Build a focused dashboard that surfaces latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) and error rates split by model and API route, with an explicit breakdown for streaming vs non-streaming request paths. Goal is to make it easy for SREs and platform engineers to: 1) quickly identify regressions tied to streaming IO, 2) correlate latency spikes with trace spans and log markers, and 3) provide cohort filters for request shape (token_count, conversation_length, prompt_prefix). This ticket covers queries, panel layout, instrumentation gaps (trace hook tags and log enrichment), metric rollups, and chart annotations for rollouts/canaries.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard shows p50/p95/p99 and error-rate panels for each model x route matrix
Each panel has a toggle to split streaming vs non-streaming and to apply cohort filters (token_count buckets, conversation_length, client_tier)
Panels include links to representative traces and a small sample of logs for any selected timeslice
Metric pipeline backfill for the last 90 days for produced percentiles is available and validated
Runbook snippet and alert thresholds (p95 > 600ms or p99 > 1.2s for high-traffic routes) documented in the ticket
Dashboards reviewed and approved by Observability PM and SRE on staging and promoted to prod
tasks: Define query templates for p50/p95/p99 using aggregated histograms vs direct percentile computation
Add trace hook tag "io_mode" (streaming|nonstreaming) and ensure it's emitted in ingestion path
Enrich logs with conversation_shape metadata (token_count, turn_count, prefix_hash)
Implement Grafana panels + templating variables for model, route, and cohort buckets
Create backfill job for histogram percentile metrics for last 90 days and run in staging
Add dashboard links to route-level rollout pages and e2e test to ensure no regressions
notes: We intentionally use a conversation-velocity framing to highlight differing latency characteristics for short-burst vs long-chat flows.
Prefer histogram aggregation (TDigest/HdrHistogram) at ingestion to avoid tail inaccuracies from sampling.
Streaming paths often show lower p50 but higher p99 due to connection warmup — dashboard should surface both simultaneously.
Plan to reuse existing trace link patterns (trace://<id>) in panel detail views so engineers can jump to traces from the chart.
Consider exposing a dataset of 'representative requests' per cohort for deeper offline analysis (separate follow-up ticket).
